---
title: "Scheduling workflows"
---

## Purpose

The scheduler creates local recurring alarms for ODK/Kobo forms, online web forms, direct ResearchOS capabilities and saved ResearchOS protocols. It uses cron-style timing, notification reminders and configurable retry intervals.

The intended round trip is:

```text
ResearchOS scheduler
    → launches the relevant form, web form, capability or protocol
    → the user completes the task
    → ResearchOS captures the result
    → outputs are returned, copied or exported
```

## Distinguish scheduling from form launch

The ODK form launcher opens a selected form and observes its return. The scheduler decides when a target should be launched.

See:

- [Scheduler capability](capabilities/scheduler-capability.qmd)
- [ODK form launcher](capabilities/odk-form-launcher.qmd)

## Field testing

Scheduled workflows should be tested on the actual device model because Android background restrictions vary by manufacturer.

Test at least:

- device unlocked and locked;
- ResearchOS in the background;
- notifications permitted and denied;
- airplane mode;
- device restart;
- the EDC already open;
- recurring schedules;
- retry behaviour.

## Schedule transfer

The supplied scheduler documentation also defines RIL schedule export and import, including transfer through QR or NFC dependency boundaries.

## Protocol runs

Schedules can now target saved protocols from the ResearchOS protocol library. A protocol is an ordered chain of saved capability presets. When a scheduled protocol runs, each step is launched in order and the outputs are written into one protocol output folder.

Protocol exports use a single `researchos_submission_id` across all steps. The canonical JSON contains a `steps` array, so downstream code can treat the protocol run as one submission while still inspecting each step independently.

## Practical notes

- Use **Test** to verify a schedule or protocol chain before relying on it in the field.
- If a protocol includes interactive capabilities, the user must complete each step before the next step can continue.
- For direct ResearchOS protocols, prefer output export over clipboard if the result will be used as study data.
- Android background notification behaviour varies by device; always test on the field device model.
